//: Duplication over the hand-written surface inside the vendored tree — every `**/tauri/**`
directory under `src/vs`, which `npm run dup` cannot see because its config ignores `src/vs`.
`scripts/dup-tauri.mjs` discovers the directories and passes them as positional arguments; this
file is only the knobs and the reading behind the number.
**`maxLines` is set, and it is not a preference — it is the fix for a silent false pass.**
jscpd's default is 1000 lines and a file over it is dropped from the scan with no message: it
leaves the file count, the denominator and the clone list, so the run reads exactly like a
clean one. `keymap.ts` crossed 1000 lines when the `mac` column was added and the gate stopped
seeing the largest hand-written file in the tree — 69 files where the directories hold 70, a
denominator 1,046 lines short, and the clone inside that file unreported. The same shape as a
scan with no paths at all, which is why both gates check their file count.
**`maxSize` closes the same defect one default over** — jscpd drops a file over 100 kB just as
silently. Nothing in this corpus is near that today, which is exactly when a trap of this kind is
cheap to close: `.jscpd.json` had three files over it and no way of knowing.
SURVIVORS — six clones, 64 lines, and every one of them is a body this fork is not free to
reshape. `src/vs/**/tauri/**` is a *port* surface: the rule the fork is built on is import if you
can, and otherwise copy the body rather than the shape (`CLAUDE.md`). Four of these are upstream
VS Code's own duplication arriving with the copy, and collapsing one buys a divergence this fork
then carries through every upgrade.
* `services/search/tauri/rawSearchService.ts` (15 lines) — `fileSearch` and `textSearch`, whose
emitter, cancelable promise and error arm are identical in upstream's own
`services/search/node/rawSearchService.ts`. This is the file `CLAUDE.md` names as the one that
was rewritten instead of copied once, and the rewrite lost behaviour that took three rounds to
find. It is a copy now, and it stays one.
* `platform/terminal/tauri/terminalEnvironment.ts`, three blocks (30 lines) — the `bash.exe`,
`bash`, `pwsh` and `zsh` arms of `getShellIntegrationInjection`, which restate the same
argument-cloning and `VSCODE_STABLE` tail in upstream's own
`platform/terminal/node/terminalEnvironment.ts`, arm for arm. The brief that ordered this
reading guessed they were one helper; they are upstream's shape, so they are not.
* `contrib/sapling/tauri/saplingCommitInfoViewPane.ts` against `saplingViewPane.ts` (14 lines)
— the ten `ViewPane` services and the `super(...)` call that passes them on. VS Code's
parameter-decorator DI reads the *leaf* constructor, so a subclass cannot inherit its base's
injections; every `ViewPane` subclass in the vendored tree restates this block, and an
intermediate class would restate it too and add one.
* `browser/tauri/keymap.ts` (5 lines) — the `Shift+Tab` halves of the two cycling rows,
`tscode.focusPreviousView` and `workbench.action.previousEditor`. They match on `scope`,
`whileEditing`, the two chords and the opening of the `mac` column, and diverge at the id, the
guard and both reasons. The table's own rule is that a key is written out as a literal rather
than produced by a loop or a shared constant, because the page that lists every key is
generated from this array and a name in place of a chord hides the chord from it.
Both duplication gates report a non-zero file count and are checked for it: a `jscpd` run with
no scan paths analyses 0 files and exits 0, which is a silent false pass.
**0.40 became 0.43 when the scan started seeing the whole tree**, and that is the one direction
this number is allowed to move for a reason other than a collapse. It is not slack: the six
clones behind it are read and justified one at a time above, and four of them are verbatim
upstream bodies that this fork exists to copy rather than restate. The figure it replaces was
measured over a scan that was missing 1,046 lines, so it was never the true one.
